name: Datavant
desc:
Health Information Specialist I | $15/hr | Full-Time, Listed as Remote but May Require Travel Between Sites, Inbound and Outbound Calls, Data Entry Heavy, No Sales Expected
Company: Datavant
Industry: Health Science

What Your Day Will Look Like:
You'll be the person who makes sure patients, doctors, insurance companies, and attorneys get the right medical records, safely and on time. You'll process requests for patient health information, pull the records, and send them out the right way while following HIPAA privacy rules. You'll prepare new patient charts, put records in the correct order, scan paper documents into the electronic health record, and check that everything is accurate and complete. You'll also answer inbound and outbound calls, and you may help with faxes, mail, data entry, scheduling pick-ups, and patient walk-ins. The work is measured on daily productivity, so accuracy and steady pace both matter.

Soft Skills
- Attention to detail
- Respect for privacy and confidentiality
- Organization
- Clear phone and written communication
- Reliability
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements

Education Minimum: High school diploma or GED
Required Experience: None listed
Preferred Experience: Healthcare setting, production or metric-based work, in-person customer service, and building relationships with on-site clients

Required Skills:
- Must be at least 18
- Basic computer skills
- Comfortable with phones, fax machines, printers, and office equipment
- Professional spoken and written English
- Able to travel between locations as needed
- Able to work overtime during peak seasons

This role is ideal for someone who:
- Wants an entry-level way into healthcare with only a HS diploma or GED
- Is detail-focused and takes privacy seriously
- Has done office, front desk, or medical records work
- Can travel to client sites if needed

Not a Good Fit for someone who:
- Needs a fully work-from-home job with no travel
- Can't meet post-offer health screening or vaccine requirements
- Can't work overtime during busy seasons
- Struggles with fast, numbers-driven work
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
1. Submit application
2. Expect an assessment email
3. Watch for an email inviting you to a prescreening
4. Depending on how well the prescreening went, expect an email to schedule an interview
This is an estimated process.

Top 10 Resume Keywords
- Release of information (ROI)
- Medical records processing
- HIPAA compliance
- Patient chart preparation
- Electronic health records (EHR)
- Document scanning and indexing
- Data entry
- Confidentiality
- Inbound and outbound calls
- Meeting productivity goals

4-5 Interview Questions for this Role:
- Tell us about your experience handling confidential or sensitive information.
- How do you stay accurate when you're working through a high volume of requests?
- A caller asks for a patient's records but can't verify who they are. What do you do?
- Tell us about a time you caught a mistake before it caused a problem. What happened, what did you do, and what was the result?
- Tell us about a time you had to meet a daily goal or quota. What was the goal, what did you do, and how did it turn out?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
-Pay: $15/hr
-Shift: Must have availability for any shift based on business needs. Can be discussed in final interview, offer stage. Overtime may be required during peak seasons.
-Benefits: Basic benefits: insurance options, PTO, possible 401k. An earlier Datavant posting listed PTO, health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k savings plan, and tuition assistance.
-Equipment Provided: Not stated in this posting. An earlier Datavant posting for this title said a computer, monitor, and virtual phone were provided.
-Felony Friendly?: Case by case
-Drug Test: Certain positions
-Notes: The posting says Remote - United States, but it also asks for the ability to commute between locations, mentions patient walk-ins, and lists in-person customer service and on-site clients as pluses. Participants should ask in the interview whether the job is fully remote or based at a client site. Many client sites require a post-offer health screening and proof of vaccines like flu, Tdap, and COVID-19, and exemptions are reviewed case by case. Training length and camera requirements are not listed.
-Career Pathway: Reasonable inferred path: Health Information Specialist I → Health Information Specialist II → Release of Information Lead → Health Information Management Supervisor. This role builds medical records, HIPAA, and EHR skills.
